landing.define.title: What is a Guidance Credibility Index?
landing.define.p1: GCI is a 0–100 score of promise-keeping against a company's own quantified guidance — revenue bands, margins, volumes, capex. It tracks that promise, not forecast accuracy, sentiment, or share price.
landing.define.p2: Each guided number gets one outcome once the period closes:
landing.method.title: How we build a score
landing.method.sources.title: Sources
landing.method.sources.text: NSE and BSE filings, company IR decks and guidance tables, earnings-call transcripts.
landing.method.guidance.title: What counts as guidance
landing.method.guidance.text: A number or range for a named metric and period, taken from a filing, results release or call transcript. Commentary without a number is left out. If guidance is raised or cut during the year, we score against the original number and show every revision next to it.
landing.method.review.title: Verification
landing.method.review.text: One analyst checks every extracted row against its source document before it counts. Scores published today are that single review. Each row keeps the quote, the document link and the date.
landing.method.score.title: Scoring
landing.method.score.text: GCI scores promise-keeping, not forecast accuracy. Each closed result earns 0–100 points for where the result landed against its own guided range: 100 inside the range, fewer the further outside. A revenue-growth miss and a margin miss share that scale when each is the same distance outside its own range. A wide range reaches 100 more easily than a tight one. Misses lose points faster than beats. A company's score is the evidence-weighted average of its metrics — a metric counts in proportion to how many closed years it has (up to five), and a metric with a single closed year is shown as context, not scored, once a deeper metric exists. Recent years weigh more. Scores are not adjusted by sector. Open periods don't count until results are filed, and a score only changes after an analyst reviews a new filing; every change is listed in the changelog.

about.what.title: What it is
about.what.p1: CiteAlpha is a product of Ocotillo Innovation Private Limited. It delivers the Guidance Credibility Index (GCI) — a 0–100 score of whether Indian listed-company management delivered on quantified guidance. It is a credit score for promises vs actuals, not a sentiment dashboard and not a price terminal.
about.what.li1: Every citeable score links to period, metric, guided band, actual, label, and source (URL + quote + citation id).
about.what.li2: India beachhead: Sensex-depth hand-labeled evidence first; broader NSE/BSE listings are navigable with honest quality badges.
about.what.li3: Explicit non-goals: no Buy / Hold / Sell, no retail tips, no OMS or live quotes.
about.why.title: Why it is needed
about.why.lede: Desks already have news, filings search, and market terminals. What they still lack is a durable, evidence-linked answer to: did this management keep its word?
about.why.drift.title: Guidance drifts
about.why.drift.text: Bands move mid-year; “dropped” reiterates vanish from memory. Without a thread of statements → actuals, miss patterns stay anecdotal.
about.why.india.title: India-shaped disclosure
about.why.india.text: NSE/BSE IR tables, mixed-language concalls, and local formats need a local spine — not a US-first product with India as an afterthought.
about.why.compliance.title: Compliance posture
about.why.compliance.text: Factual delivery research stays on the right side of SEBI RA risk. Analysts own forecasts; the platform shows observed delivery and citations.
about.why.hitl.title: HITL that compounds
about.why.hitl.text: Extract → review → commit turns desk corrections into a lasting corpus — not a one-off paste into a spreadsheet.
about.how.title: How it works
about.how.lede: One pipeline: ingest → structure → searchable → citable. Citability is not a bolt-on — it only works when documents are stored with structure preserved.
about.pipeline.1.title: Ingest
about.pipeline.1.text: IR pages, transcripts, and filings land in the document store — Sensex crawl first; paste is the exception path.
about.pipeline.2.title: Extract & review
about.pipeline.2.text: Quantified guidance becomes pending statements. Analysts Accept / Edit / Reject before anything enters GCI math.
about.pipeline.3.title: Match & score
about.pipeline.3.text: Guidance bands meet reported actuals. Labels: met, exceeded, missed, dropped, pending — then a 0–100 company GCI.
about.pipeline.4.title: Cite
about.pipeline.4.text: Every citeable score point carries period, metric, quote, URL, and citation id bound to an accepted document.
about.how.note: Data quality stays honest: Hand-labeled for external citation; Provisional listings are scored for screening only — never invent citeable quotes. Analytics overlays (e.g. GCI vs tape) are descriptive patterns, not forecasts. Granger panels show statistical precedence only.
about.layers.title: Capability layers
about.layers.lede: These are product capability layers, not commercial plans. Seats and API access live on Package. Annotated screenshots: tier gallery.
about.layers.foundation.title: Foundation
about.layers.foundation.text: Auto ingest → period docs (transcript / results / IR) → entity search with corpus honesty → citeable citation ids. Analyst Workbench → Corpus builds the Sensex gate.
about.layers.workflow.title: Workflow
about.layers.workflow.text: Multi-horizon Δ (QoQ/YoY from PIT), GCI↔price descriptive overlays, private notes, role report templates with citation appendix.
about.layers.analytics.title: Analytics (gated)
about.layers.analytics.text: LASSO → Granger F-test and FDR impact map on ≥12-quarter PIT series. Not causation, not a forecast — methodology card on the dossier Analytics panel.

about.layers.oos.text: Buy/Hold/Sell, treating provisional listing scores as citeable IR evidence, or cloning a global market-intel OS in product chrome.

method.page.title: How the Guidance Credibility Index is built
method.page.lede: GCI is a 0–100 score of promise-keeping: how reliably reported results landed against the numbers management guided to. It measures that promise — not forecast accuracy, not sentiment, not share price, and not whether results were good news.
method.page.guidance.title: 1. What counts as guidance
method.page.guidance.i1: A number or range for a named metric and a named period — for example "revenue growth of 13%–15% in constant currency for FY23".
method.page.guidance.i2: It must come from a primary source: an exchange filing (NSE, BSE, or the SEC for dual-listed companies), a company results release or investor deck, or an earnings-call transcript.
method.page.guidance.i3: Commentary without a number ("we expect a strong year") is recorded as unmapped and never scored.
method.page.review.title: 2. Review before anything is scored
method.page.review.i1: An analyst checks each extracted guidance row and each actual against its source document before the row counts. Every row keeps the exact quote, the document link and the date.
method.page.review.i2: Only companies whose rows have all been reviewed and cited carry a score. Companies with sample data or no reviewed guidance show "Not yet scored".
method.page.review.i3: A score changes only after an analyst reviews a new filing. Nothing updates automatically from a news feed or a model. For filings dated on or after 29 Sep 2026, the reviewed score is published within 5 business days of the results filing.
method.page.review.i4: Scores published today were reviewed by one analyst. A second reviewer is required when a new row is submitted and then accepted by a different person; an account admin may accept their own submission. A monthly sample audit by a second reviewer, and its pass rate on the Trust Center, will be published once that audit is running. Until then the published index is single-analyst review.
method.page.sla.title: Filing to score
method.page.sla.target: Target: a reviewed score published within {days} business days of the results filing (India Monday–Friday), for filings dated on or after {since}.
method.page.sla.live: Observed (live sample): median {median} business days across {n} rows.
method.page.sla.liveEmpty: Observed (live sample): none yet — no filings dated on or after {since} have been scored.
method.page.sla.backfill: Historical batch ({n} rows, reviewed {reviewedOn}): median {median} business days from the original results filing to that review. Those rows were labeled after the fact and are not measured against the 5-day target.
method.page.revisions.title: 3. When guidance is raised or cut during the year
method.page.revisions.p1: The score uses the original guidance — the number management gave at the start of the period. That is the promise investors priced in, and the question GCI asks is whether it held.
method.page.revisions.p2: Every later revision is recorded next to the original with its own date and source, along with a second outcome measured against the final revised range. That second outcome is shown for context and is not part of the score. A revision is not treated as withdrawn guidance.
method.page.revisions.example: Example: Infosys guided FY23 revenue growth of 13%–15%, raised it three times to 16.0%–16.5%, and delivered 15.4%. Against the original range that is exceeded; against the final range it is missed. Both are shown on the company page:
method.page.formula.title: 4. Scoring one result
method.page.formula.intro: Each closed result (guidance plus its reported actual) earns 0–100 points:
method.page.formula.inside.label: Inside the guided range:
method.page.formula.inside.text: 100 points. A single-number guide gets a ±2% range around it.
method.page.formula.outside.label: Outside the range:
method.page.formula.outside.text1: we measure the distance outside in units of the range's half-width, δ. Points decay as
method.page.formula.outside.text2: , so small misses cost a little and large misses cost a lot.
method.page.formula.beats.label: Beats
method.page.formula.beats.text: (above the range) decay from 100 toward a floor of 60 and never go below it.
method.page.formula.misses.label: Misses
method.page.formula.misses.text: (below the range) lose points 1.4 times as fast and can reach 0.
method.page.formula.philosophy: GCI measures promise-keeping discipline, not forecast accuracy. A company that beats by a wide margin is scored on how reliable its promise was, not how much upside it delivered.
method.page.formula.floor.label: Why the floor of 60 for beats?
method.page.formula.floor.text: A wide beat scores below 100 because the result landed outside the original range. Under-promising is a smaller credibility problem than over-promising, so any beat stays at or above 60, and a material miss can reach 0. The floor of 60 is a design choice.
method.page.formula.constants.label: Why these numbers?
method.page.formula.constants.text: A miss one half-width outside the guided range scores about 59, about 41 points below a result inside the range, because misses lose points 1.4 times as fast as the underlying decay. A beat the same distance scores about 88 and stays at or above 60. A single-number guide is treated as a ±2% range around that number. Withdrawing guidance deducts 15 points, a restatement deducts 15, and conflicting guidance for the same period deducts 10. The most recent year weighs 1.0, the year before 0.86, then 0.74. These constants are design choices, published so a reader can judge them.
method.page.formula.example: Example: Infosys guided FY22 revenue growth of 12%–14% (midpoint 13%, half-width 1 point) and grew 19.7%. That is 5.7 half-widths above the range, so the row scores about 62. A miss the same distance below the range would score 0.
method.page.company.title: 5. From results to a company score
method.page.company.metric.label: Per metric:
method.page.company.metric.text: a weighted average of that metric's results. The most recent year has weight 1.0, the year before 0.86, then 0.74, and so on. Rows labeled with lower source confidence count slightly less.
method.page.company.company.label: Per company:
method.page.company.company.text: the evidence-weighted average of its metric scores. Each metric's weight equals its number of closed reporting periods, capped at five. A metric with only one closed period is shown as context and does not enter the score when another metric has two or more; if every metric has a single period, the score is a plain average and carries the provisional tier.
method.page.company.deductions.label: Deductions:
method.page.company.deductions.text: 15 points if guidance was withdrawn, 15 points for a restatement, and 10 points when two reviewed rows give conflicting guidance for the same guidance thread and period.
method.page.company.open.label: Open periods
method.page.company.open.text: (guidance given, results not yet filed) are shown as pending and not counted.
method.page.company.history: Every score carries a confidence tier: provisional (fewer than three closed periods, or one metric), established (three or more periods, two or more metrics) or deep (five or more periods, two or more metrics). A metric counts toward breadth once it has one closed, analyst-reviewed result, whether it enters the composite or is shown as context. A closed result scores only when both the original guidance and the subsequent actual are cited; rows missing the guidance citation are shown as pending guidance cite and do not enter the score. Only established and deep scores are ranked on the Public Snapshot. Most scored companies are provisional today.
method.page.company.record: Next to the score we show the delivery record — how many results came in above, inside, or below guidance — so the direction of any miss is visible separately from the score.
method.page.company.comparable.label: Across metrics and sectors
method.page.company.comparable.text: A revenue-growth miss and a margin miss share the 0–100 scale when each is the same distance outside its own guided range, measured in that range's half-width. A wide range reaches 100 more easily than a tight one. Scores are not adjusted by sector. A sector average is the average of the company scores in that sector, not a claim that a 70 in one sector is the same operating result as a 70 in another.
method.page.independence.title: 6. Independence
method.page.independence.text: Payment never influences a score or when it changes. Covered companies cannot buy, edit or delay their score. A company that subscribes to {product} for IR or compliance work gets the same read access as any other customer.
method.page.errors.title: 7. Reporting an error
method.page.errors.before: If you think a row is wrong, email
method.page.errors.after: with the company, period and the source you are relying on. We re-check the original filing; if the row is wrong we correct it, and the score updates when the dataset is rebuilt.

ui.TierFeaturesPage.tier3.intro: UI is EXPERIMENTAL. Engine: LASSO → Granger F-test on PIT warehouse (≥12 quarters). VAR held until ≥24. Still descriptive precedence — not causation.
ui.TierFeaturesPage.ask-8.title: Lead / lag factor analysis
ui.TierFeaturesPage.ask-8.body: Dependent = GCI; independents = metrics & price tape. LASSO selects candidates; Granger reports F, p, best lag.
ui.TierFeaturesPage.ask-9.title: Impact factor mapping
ui.TierFeaturesPage.ask-9.body: Directed edges only where Granger passes FDR control. Empty map when no significant edges (as on INFY in this capture).
ui.TierFeaturesPage.method1.name: Cross-Correlation Function (CCF)
ui.TierFeaturesPage.method1.role: Correlation at different lags. Cheap and interpretable; can invent lag peaks via autocorrelation.
ui.TierFeaturesPage.method1.stance: Shipped as aid under Granger rows — not the causal claim.
ui.TierFeaturesPage.method2.name: Granger causality
ui.TierFeaturesPage.method2.role: Does X’s past improve Y beyond Y’s own past? Recognizable to institutional analysts; needs stationarity.
ui.TierFeaturesPage.method2.stance: Tier 3 v1 — shipped (LASSO → F-test, N gate, experimental badge).
ui.TierFeaturesPage.method3.name: VAR / VECM
ui.TierFeaturesPage.method3.role: Joint multi-series dynamics for richer impact maps. Needs longer aligned series.
ui.TierFeaturesPage.method4.name: LASSO / Elastic Net
ui.TierFeaturesPage.method4.role: Variable selection — shrink irrelevant candidates before Granger/VAR.
ui.TierFeaturesPage.method4.stance: Shipped as the front step of Granger v1.
ui.TierFeaturesPage.method5.name: Transfer entropy
ui.TierFeaturesPage.method5.role: Model-free directional information flow; opaque and data-hungry.
ui.TierFeaturesPage.method6.name: Causal graphical models (PC / DAG)
ui.TierFeaturesPage.method6.role: Infer a full impact network. Brittle assumptions; wrong arrows destroy trust.
ui.TierFeaturesPage.title: Tier 1–3 features
ui.TierFeaturesPage.lede: Annotated product walkthrough with live captures (INFY · Sensex hand-labeled pilot). Surfaces are real; experimental analytics stay in the Workbench and are not citeable. No Buy / Hold.
ui.TierFeaturesPage.methodology.title: Methodology options (#8 / #9)
ui.TierFeaturesPage.methodology.intro: Locked path: stationarity gates → LASSO → Granger → optional CCF aid → VAR when N allows. Transfer entropy and causal DAGs stay out of customer-facing v1.

ui.TrustPage.tenancyFallback: org_id isolation for reviews, seats, and API keys.
ui.TrustPage.llmNote: Optional extract model with heuristic fallback. Customer extract text may be sent to a contracted processor when enabled.

ui.TrustPage.labelingFallback: Scores published today were reviewed by one analyst. A second reviewer applies to newly submitted rows.

ui.TrustPage.sourceLinksFailed: {failed} recorded quotes were not on the filing; those rows are not citeable until re-cited.

tier.provisional.title: Fewer than three closed reporting periods, or one metric with a closed result. Shown, not ranked.
tier.established.title: Three or more closed periods, and two or more metrics with a closed result (composite or context). Ranked.
tier.deep.title: Five or more closed periods, and two or more metrics with a closed result (composite or context). Ranked.
tier.depth: {periods} closed period(s) · {metrics} metric(s) with a closed result

dossier.calc.title: How this score is calculated
dossier.deltasPending: Score changes appear after 4 reviewed reporting dates ({n} so far).
dossier.experimentalBanner: Experimental — synthetic inputs. Not part of the published GCI.
changelog.title: Score changelog
changelog.lede: Every change to a published Guidance Credibility Index level — new filing, data correction, flag change or method revision — is listed here the day it ships. The score ledger holds one row per published level and is never edited.
changelog.ledger.title: Score ledger
changelog.ledger.lede: Published levels, newest first. Each row names the algorithm, dataset version and reviewer.
screener.notScored.tip: Not yet scored — no analyst-reviewed guidance yet.
screener.filter.unscoredNote: {n} not yet scored — untick to show them (sorted last).
screener.filter.noneScored: No scored companies in this list yet. Untick “Scored only” to see the full membership.
rankings.noneRankable: No company has reached the established tier yet (three closed reporting periods across two or more metrics). Provisional scores are published on each company page but are not ranked.

products.get.screener.title: GCI Screener
products.get.screener.text: Screen Indian listed companies by how reliably reported results kept their own guidance.
products.get.workbench.title: Analyst Workbench
products.get.workbench.text: Review extracted guidance, check sources, and export cited reports. Requires a pilot or Desk seat.
products.get.search.title: Filing Search
products.get.search.text: Search filings and transcripts; cite-only answers bound to primary sources.
products.get.api.title: API / Data
products.get.api.text: Point-in-time GCI reads under /api/v1. Quote for Enterprise.
products.skuAppendix.lede: Score, Cite, Radar, Ledger, and Data describe jobs on the same disclosure spine. Commercial access is Pilot, Desk seat, or Enterprise API.
help.walkthrough.title: Product walkthrough
help.walkthrough.lede: Annotated captures of Screener, dossier, evidence, and Workbench. The long-form page remains at /about/tiers.
developers.title: CiteAlpha API
developers.lede: Public reads live under /api/v1. OpenAPI is at /docs. Write and operations routes are not listed on the public spec.
status.title: Service status
status.lede: Live health of the GCI API and the latest published index file.
trust.linkOut.title: Link-out policy
trust.linkOut.body: Filings and transcripts stay on the issuer or exchange site. CiteAlpha stores a dated quote and a link; we do not redistribute original PDFs. Public pages do not show vendor prices — GCI does not use prices as an input.
trust.refund.title: Cancellation
trust.refund.body: Pilot seats are complimentary and end on the agreed date. Paid Desk and Enterprise contracts cancel per the order form; unused prepaid time after the notice period is refunded on a pro-rata basis unless the order form says otherwise.
